headline: Easy-run efficiency is holding into the 20 km work, but this block still hasn't tested a genuinely hard effort.
confidence_reasons: Limited data sources active in last 3 days
summary:
Your comparable-effort easy runs continue to sit in a lower HR band than the prior period, and yesterday's 11 km fits that pattern cleanly — controlled, almost entirely sub-threshold, with only a token minute of Z3. Across a doubled four-week block that efficiency has stayed intact rather than eroding under the added load, which is the signal that matters most right now. Strength has also become genuinely consistent, running at more than double the prior block's session count, so this isn't endurance volume crowding out the rest of your athletic base.

The open question hasn't changed: the easy-run picture is strong, but the last few weeks have been built almost entirely from Z1–Z2. You've accumulated durability and time on feet, but no threshold or sustained-hard effort has stress-tested whether that lower HR band survives real intensity. That's not a gap to force this week — with St. Olavsleden roughly two weeks out, staying aerobic and durable is the right call — but it's worth naming that current fitness is well-evidenced on the easy end and largely unproven at the top end.

With the crossing approaching, the more relevant readiness gap is specificity: loaded pack-carry and sustained vertical remain absent from what the data shows, and those are the demands a 6–8 kg self-supported hilly trail will actually impose.
watch_items: Whether any loaded-pack or sustained-climbing work appears before the crossing, given the terrain and pack weight ahead.
Whether the lower easy-run HR band holds once daily back-to-back-style fatigue accumulates on trail.
Whether sleep duration stabilises, since consecutive long days will make recovery quality matter more than it does now.
Whether Polar's strain window ever catches up to actual load, or the implausible DETRAINING label simply persists and should be ignored.

evidence_items.text: ▲ 4-week volume 189 km vs 97 km prior block (+95%)
▼ Easy-run HR averaging 142 bpm vs 151 bpm prior period (comparable-effort runs, 11 vs 5 runs)
